Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the NovaMart Q1 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to NovaMart's Q1 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Alex Rivera, CEO; Jordan Lee, CFO; Taylor Kim, COO; Riley Patel, CMO; Casey Nguyen, CTO; Morgan Ellis, CDO; and Jordan Reyes, CSO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, CEO of NovaMart.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q1 performance, driven by accelerating GMV growth across our multi-category marketplace and resilient consumer demand in core verticals like fashion, electronics, and home goods. We saw significant growth in key metrics, with GMV up 25% year-over-year to $4.2 billion, active customers expanding 18% to 45 million, and mobile orders now representing 62% of total volume.

Our focus remains on scaling our private-label offerings and leveraging AI for personalized experiences. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our quick-commerce groceries vertical, which we believe will significantly expand our addressable market into ultra-fast delivery segments.

We are investing heavily in supply chain resilience and international expansion to capture share in high-growth regions.

We are focused on improving fulfillment efficiencies through our owned network.

We are expanding our presence in Europe and APAC.

We are enhancing our customer experience through dynamic pricing and recommendation engines.

Finally, we are committed to sustainability initiatives that align with consumer preferences for eco-friendly options.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Jordan Lee, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Alex. Our Q1 revenue was $2.8 billion, an increase of 28% year-over-year. Gross margin was 38.2%, up 170 basis points from 36.5% in Q1 2023 and 60 basis points sequentially from Q4 2023. This marks our sixth straight quarter of expansion, highlighting the durability of our e-commerce model as we approach $15 billion in annual run-rate GMV. For reference, we calculate gross margin as net revenue minus cost of goods sold—or COGS—divided by net revenue, with COGS encompassing product acquisition, inbound freight, packaging, and fulfillment, while outbound shipping sits in operating expenses to align with peers like Amazon and Shopify.

Diving deeper into gross margin trends, we've shown steady gains despite inflation in global supply chains. Comparing quarters: Q1 2023 at 36.5%, Q2 up 30 basis points to 36.8% on private-label ramp-up, Q3 to 37.2% with fulfillment scale, Q4 to 37.6% on holiday mix, and now Q1 2024 at 38.2% thanks to AI pricing and better supplier terms. That 170 basis point YoY lift added about $250 million to the bottom line, outperforming pure-play e-tailers around 35-37% and narrowing the gap to Amazon's 43% in North America retail.

Key positives included a favorable product mix shift contributing 60 basis points, with private labels at 28% of GMV—up from 22%—delivering 45% margins versus 32% on third-party sales. Our Nova Essentials in home goods and apparel, sourced directly from sustainable mills in Vietnam and India, hit over 50% margins, much like Amazon Basics. We trimmed low-margin electronics to 18% of mix using our AI Dynamic Catalog Engine for high-margin SKUs. Quick-commerce groceries, at a $2.5 billion run-rate, improved to 22% margins from 18% with premium pricing on under-15-minute deliveries in 12 metros.

Supply chain efficiencies added 70 basis points: inventory turns at 8.2x from 7.1x enabled 12-15% better terms from suppliers like P&G and Unilever, inbound freight down 8% to $1.45 per unit via Vendor-Managed Inventory covering 40% of SKUs. Our ML Demand Sensing on AWS SageMaker cut stockouts 25% and writedowns $45 million. Blockchain with IBM Food Trust reduced grocery spoilage 15%.

Fulfillment optimization contributed 40 basis points: 35 owned centers and 5,000 partner lockers handled 85% in-house, dropping 3PL reliance to 18%. Same-day penetration at 45% in cities, utilization 92%, yielding $0.75 per unit profit.

Headwinds were limited to a net 10 basis point drag: Red Sea issues spiked freight 10% QoQ, adding $0.12 per unit, mitigated by Cape routing and hedges. Promo intensity to 22% of GMV from free shipping over $35 was offset by dynamic pricing recapturing 60% via upsells, lifting AOV to $52 from $49.

Regionally, North America at 60% revenue and 40.1% GM benefited from Nova Unlimited subs at 65 million. Europe at 37.5% GM improved 100 basis points with localized fashion. APAC emerging at 34.8% GM grew groceries 150% YoY.

Looking forward, Q2 margins at 38.5-39.0%, full-year 38.5% with levers like owned manufacturing for 10% private labels, $150 million GenAI for bidding, eco-packaging savings, and e-commerce penetration upside.

Operating expenses were $1.9 billion, representing 68% of revenue. Marketing spend moderated as efficiencies took hold, with CAC at $25 reflecting better ROAS from targeted campaigns.

Our net income for the quarter was $285 million, up 42% year-over-year from $200 million, beating our $240 million guidance midpoint and consensus $248 million. Diluted EPS was $1.78, up 39% from $1.28, topping $1.55 guidance and $1.62 estimates. Full-year net income on track for record highs, reflecting our marketplace strength with 2 million sellers and $45 billion annual GMV.

This beat stemmed from 28% revenue growth on 32% GMV to $12.5 billion quarterly pace, take rate to 18.2%, AOV to $85 via AI upsells boosting cross-sell 22%. Gross margins hit 72.5% on fulfillment down to 14.2% of GMV through our NovaMart Logistics Network with 1,200 partners and 65% same-day urban delivery. Nova Unlimited added $450 million recurring.

Expenses grew 18% to $2.1 billion but below guide, CAC to $22 with LTV $450 for 20x ratio, marketing to 22% revenue. North America surged 50% net income on holiday peaks, Europe 38%, APAC 65% via expansions.

Promotional activities powerfully drove sales, contributing 42% of 28% GMV growth to $2.85 billion, with 35% order surge from Flash Deals at 20-50% off electronics, apparel, home. Site-wide events like Summer Tech Blitz generated $1.2 billion GMV, conversions to 4.2%, personalized banners up CTR 18%. U.S. 48% promo GMV, Europe 22% localized, APAC 45% with free shipping boosting repeats 28%.

Profitability held with 320 basis point GM dip to 37.8% from 22% discounts and $150 million shipping waivers, but ROAS 5.2x via PromoOptix ML testing 1,200 variants, targeting high-LTV. EBITDA margins to 11.2% on turnover 8.2x, direct fulfillment cuts. Evolving to loyalty-tied promos lifting retention 14%, value engineering private labels.

On logistics and shipping, costs hit $285 million, 12.8% revenue up 18% YoY from disruptions. Ocean rates up 25-30% to $4,200 FEU on Red Sea adding 10-14 days, port backlogs 20-25%, fuel 12%, GRIs 8-10%. Compressed logistics GM 220 bps to 4.1%.

Mitigations: SmartShip AI cut failures 22%, 7% costs; five new MFCs with robotics for 40% same-day, 12-15% savings; Flexport commitments, drone pilots. Nearshoring 28% from China to Vietnam/Mexico/India. Q3 moderation to +8-10% YoY.

AOV trended to $58.40 trailing 12 months, +14.7% YoY, Q1 $56.20 +12.1%, Q2 pace $58.40 +15.2%. Personalization up cross-sell 28%, bundles add-ons to 2.1; free shipping threshold $55 added $2.10; OmniPrime at $78.40 AOV. Dynamic pricing value packs +19% electronics. Headwinds: inflation dipped home goods 2.4%, competition capped some.

International expansion hit $2.8 billion GMV, 28% total +52% YoY. Europe $1.4 billion +48%, 12 million MAUs UK/Germany, AOV $85, conversions 4.2%, DHL next-day. APAC $850 million +78%, India $400 million +95%, SEA $450 million +65%, live-stream 15% orders. LATAM $450 million +42%, Brazil $300 million payments integration.

Inventory for holidays at $2.5 billion +18% YoY, DIOH 45 days, turnover 8.2x. Q4 GMV $4.8 billion +22%, AOV $145, electronics 28%, fashion 20%. AI forecasting error <5%, robotics pick 400/hour, BOPIS 22%.

For guidance, Q4 revenue $2.85-2.95 billion +14-18%, GMV $11.5-12.0 billion +22-27%, EBITDA $285-310 million 10-10.5%. FY2025 revenue $11.8-12.3 billion +16-21%, GMV $48-52 billion +24-32%, EBITDA margins 11.5-12.5%. NovaAI 2.0, micro-FCs, social commerce.

We ended with $2.5 billion cash. Reaffirming full-year guidance.

Now I'll turn it over to Taylor Kim to discuss operations.

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, Jordan. Operationally, we focused on network optimization and vendor partnerships. Our shipping times improved by 25%. Fulfillment costs were down 12%. We are implementing AI-driven routing in our 35 centers.

Now I'll turn it over to Riley Patel.

Riley Patel:
Thanks, Taylor. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from Flash Deals and Summer Tech Blitz. Customer acquisition costs were $25. Our brand awareness increased by 22%. We are focusing on loyalty personalization.

Now I'll turn it over to Casey Nguyen.

Casey Nguyen:
Thanks, Riley. On the technology front, we've been focused on recommendation engines and edge computing. Our website uptime was 99.9%. Mobile app usage increased by 35%. We're investing in GenAI for pricing.

Now I'll turn it over to Morgan Ellis.

Morgan Ellis:
Thanks, Casey. Data science is a key focus for us. We've seen a 15% improvement in conversion rates because of ShopperDNA personalization. We are also focusing on GDPR-compliant privacy tools.

Now I'll turn it over to Jordan Reyes.

Jordan Reyes:
Thanks, Morgan. Sustainability is very important to us. We reduced our carbon footprint by 20%. We are committed to eco-packaging and carbon-neutral shipping pilots.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, we will now begin the question and answer session. Our first question comes from Mike Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Mike Chen:
Thanks. Jordan, can you expand on the gross margin drivers and outlook?

Alex Rivera:
Thanks, Mike. Jordan, want to take that?

Jordan Lee:
Absolutely, Alex. As I detailed earlier, the 38.2% reflects mix shift to 28% private labels at 45% margins, supply efficiencies with 8.2x turns, and fulfillment profits. Q2 at 38.5-39.0% on vertical integration and GenAI.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with JPMorgan.

Lisa Wong:
Hi team. On promotions, how did they balance sales growth with profitability?

Jordan Lee:
Great question, Lisa. Promos fueled 42% of 28% GMV growth but dipped GM 320 bps; ROAS 5.2x via PromoOptix recouped most, with EBITDA up 150 bps on scale.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Ruiz with Morgan Stanley.

David Ruiz:
Thanks. Taylor, thoughts on logistics disruptions and holiday inventory prep?

Taylor Kim:
Thanks, David. Building on Jordan's logistics comments—Red Sea added costs but SmartShip AI and nearshoring mitigated. Inventory at $2.5 billion, DIOH 45 for $4.8 billion Q4 GMV demand.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Hart with Barclays.

Emily Hart:
Hi. Riley, details on international AOV trends?

Riley Patel:
Sure, Emily. International AOV strong at $52-85 regionally, up double-digits on bundles and Prime perks, despite macro; APAC mobile bundles offset FX.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Citi.

Raj Patel:
Casey, on net income beats—what's sustainable?

Casey Nguyen:
Raj, the $285 million Q1 net income and $1.78 EPS beat on GMV momentum, 72.5% margins, CAC efficiencies—FY24 raised to $1.1-1.2 billion on tech leverage.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sophia Lee with Deutsche Bank.

Sophia Lee:
Morgan, forward guidance details?

Morgan Ellis:
Sophia, Q4 revenue $2.85-2.95 billion, GMV $11.5-12 billion, EBITDA 10-10.5%; FY25 GMV $48-52 billion on NovaAI, social, Prime growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Kevin Brooks with RBC Capital.

Kevin Brooks:
Jordan Reyes, sustainability impact on costs?

Jordan Reyes:
Kevin, our 20% carbon cut via GreenShip saved 7% packaging COGS, with neutral shipping premiums adding margins in high-LTV categories.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Anna Kim with Piper Sandler.

Anna Kim:
Team, AOV factors amid competition?

Alex Rivera:
Anna, AOV to $58.40 on personalization +28% cross-sell, $55 free ship, Prime $78; H2 gen-AI targets 10-15% more.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.

Impact of promotional activities on sales and profitability.
Holiday season preparation: Inventory levels and expected demand.
Net income and earnings per share (EPS): Performance vs. expectations.
International market expansion: Progress and performance metrics.
Logistics and shipping costs: Impact of supply chain disruptions.
Average order value (AOV) trends: Factors influencing AOV changes.
Forward guidance: Revenue, GMV, and profitability outlook.
